key_insight: ConQUESTA prunes quantum neural networks by jointly considering task accuracy, hardware topology, and compiler cost, so it can reduce entangling resources without sacrificing much performance.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum software/hardware teams a practical post-training method to make QNNs more deployable on sparse devices by lowering two-qubit gates, SWAPs, and circuit depth.
method: Screens candidate entanglers using both saliency and transpilation-aware cost.
Searches complete pruning masks under an explicit accuracy constraint instead of one-shot ranking.
Evaluates each mask as a whole across multiple coupling topologies to account for routing effects.
evidence_signal: At 55% pruning across 4-, 6-, and 8-qubit QNNs and eight seeds, ConQUESTA reduced resources by 61.6% on Breast Cancer, 72.0% on Digits01, and 82.2% on Iris, with fixed-mask recovery improving feasible runs from 16/24 to 22/24.
watch_item: The method increases search and transpilation overhead because it evaluates many complete masks and its benefits may depend on the chosen topology, resource weights, and pruning budget.
paper_title: ConQUESTA: Topology-Aware Post-Training Structural Pruning of Quantum Neural Networks
